summary: Iteration 11 — Activity History (site visits) + Admin Notification Bell fully verified. Backend: 27/27 pytest pass (14 new in test_iteration11_notifications_and_activity.py + 13 regression from test_site_visits.py). Frontend: admin bell with unread badge, dropdown click-to-navigate, mark-all-read, engineer bell hidden, and SiteVisitDetailPage Activity History card with colored action badges all behave as designed.

minor.issue: Spec says 'VISIT DELETED activity logged BEFORE the actual delete' but the code logs AFTER db.site_visits.delete_one (server.py L3776-3782). Functionally the row still ends up in activity_log so test passes — purely a code-ordering nit, not a bug.

integration_issues.issue: Notifications for site visits that were later deleted still appear in the dropdown and route to a non-existent /site-visits/<id> (404 toast + no detail page). Consider either (a) cascading delete of notifications when their visit is deleted, or (b) showing a 'visit no longer exists' state on the detail page.

verified_features: Engineer-submitted POST /site-visits writes VISIT CREATED to activity_log keyed by site_visit_id AND creates an admin-targeted notification.
Admin-submitted POST /site-visits writes VISIT CREATED but does NOT create a notification (verified by checking no notification references that visit id).
PUT /site-visits/{id} with unchanged status writes VISIT UPDATED row and does NOT fire a new notification.
PUT /site-visits/{id} flipping draft→submitted by engineer writes STATUS CHANGED activity AND fires an admin notification.
DELETE /site-visits/{id} writes VISIT DELETED activity row (still readable via /activity after the visit doc is gone).
GET /site-visits/{vid}/activity returns rows sorted by created_at DESC; route is correctly declared before /site-visits/{vid} catch-all (no 404, no wrong handler).
GET /notifications returns {items, unread} — admin sees role-targeted notifs, engineer sees 0.

POST /notifications/{nid}/read uses $addToSet → per-user read state; the marked notification stays in another user's feed as unread (verified at the model layer: read_by array contains only the acking user's id and is_read flips just for them).
POST /notifications/read-all zeros the unread count for the current user.
Frontend Admin navbar shows NotificationBell with red badge showing unread count.
Frontend Engineer navbar does NOT show NotificationBell (admin-only gate at Navbar.jsx L58: `user.role === 'admin' && <NotificationBell />`).
Clicking a notification item marks-read, navigates to /site-visits/<id>, and the dropdown closes.
'Mark all read' button optimistically clears the red badge.
SiteVisitDetailPage shows Activity History card with VISIT CREATED / VISIT UPDATED rows, colored badges, username (test_engineer) and timestamps.
action_items: (Optional / nit) Re-order delete_site_visit in server.py L3776-3782 so _log_sv_activity runs BEFORE db.site_visits.delete_one to match the spec wording (currently it logs after — functionally identical because the activity row only references site_visit_id, but it would match the documented intent).

(Recommended) Consider cascading the notifications collection when a site visit is deleted, OR gracefully render a 'visit no longer exists' state instead of a generic 404. Currently old notifications keep navigating users to detail pages that 404. Not blocking but a UX papercut.
critical_code_review_comments: _log_sv_activity and _notify_admins both swallow exceptions silently and only log — good for not breaking the user request, but make sure those logs are scraped/alerted in production, otherwise notification regressions could go unnoticed.

GET /notifications applies its $or visibility filter at the DB level then re-applies _user_can_see_notification in Python and trims to `limit`. Acceptable for current volumes; will need a proper paginated unread_count aggregation if notifications volume grows.
/app/backend/server.py is now 4194 lines — still well over the 700-line guideline. Splitting site_visits + notifications into their own modules would help (carry-over from iter10).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin bell + engineer-no-bell + activity card + mark-all-read all verified via Playwright)
